questions.name: Forklift Fundamentals and Markings
questions.objective: 1.1 Define powered industrial trucks and common forklift uses
questions.text: What is a forklift as described in powered industrial truck safety training?

answers.text: A mobile, power-driven vehicle used to carry, push, pull, lift, stack, or tier material
A hand-carried tool used only for lifting small boxes
A fixed conveyor used only to move material along one path
A passenger vehicle used primarily for transporting employees

explanations.a: A forklift is a mobile, power-driven industrial vehicle used for moving and positioning materials. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: A forklift is powered mobile equipment, not a hand-carried tool.
explanations.c: Conveyors move material on fixed paths, while forklifts are mobile vehicles.
explanations.d: Forklifts are material-handling vehicles, not personnel transport vehicles.

questions.name: Forklift Fundamentals and Markings
questions.objective: 1.1 Define powered industrial trucks and common forklift uses
questions.text: Which task is a typical forklift use?

answers.text: Lifting people without an approved work platform and controls
Tiering pallets in a warehouse or loading materials at a construction site
Using the mast as a crane without considering capacity or manufacturer limits
Transporting workers as passengers on the forks

explanations.a: Personnel lifting requires specific controls and cannot be treated as normal load handling.
explanations.b: Forklifts are commonly used to lift, stack, tier, load, unload, and move materials. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Using the forklift outside its intended limits can create instability and equipment hazards.
explanations.d: Forks are not for passenger transport.

questions.name: Forklift Fundamentals and Markings
questions.objective: 1.1 Define powered industrial trucks and common forklift uses
questions.text: During forklift operator certification training, why are forklifts a significant safety concern?

answers.text: They are safer than all other vehicles because they move indoors
They are harmless when moving slowly
They are widely used around workers and pedestrians and can create serious struck-by, tip-over, and crushing hazards
They cannot tip over when unloaded

explanations.a: Indoor operation does not remove vehicle, pedestrian, or stability hazards.
explanations.b: Slow movement can still crush or strike workers.
explanations.c: Forklifts operate near people and materials, so safe operation and pedestrian protection are critical. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Unloaded forklifts can tip, especially during turns or on uneven surfaces.

questions.name: Forklift Fundamentals and Markings
questions.objective: 1.1 Define powered industrial trucks and common forklift uses
questions.text: Which statement best describes forklift safety training purpose?

answers.text: To teach operators to bypass manufacturer instructions
To replace hands-on evaluation with a short quiz only
To allow any worker to operate any forklift without site-specific instruction
To help operators and affected workers recognize hazards and use safe work practices

explanations.a: Manufacturer warnings and precautions are part of safe operation.
explanations.b: Forklift qualification requires practical training and evaluation, not a quiz alone.
explanations.c: Operators need authorization, training, and evaluation for the equipment and workplace.
explanations.d: Forklift safety training supports safe operation, hazard recognition, and protection of operators and pedestrians. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Forklift Fundamentals and Markings
questions.objective: 1.2 Identify equipment covered and not covered by OSHA 1910.178
questions.text: Which scenario requires attention to whether OSHA 1910.178 applies?

answers.text: An operator checks pedestrian travel paths
A supervisor verifies that forklift markings are readable
A worker reads the forklift data plate before operation
An employer uses different powered vehicles and must distinguish forklifts from excluded equipment

explanations.a: Pedestrian controls are part of safe forklift operation.
explanations.b: Readable markings support safe use of covered equipment.
explanations.c: Answer boundary: reading the data plate is a safe practice for covered forklifts.
explanations.d: Employers need to know which equipment falls under powered industrial truck requirements and which equipment is outside that rule. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Forklift Fundamentals and Markings
questions.objective: 1.2 Identify equipment covered and not covered by OSHA 1910.178
questions.text: A supervisor is reviewing powered industrial truck safety. Which vehicle is generally covered by powered industrial truck rules?

answers.text: A powered forklift used to lift and move pallets
A compressed air-operated industrial truck excluded by the rule
A farm vehicle used in agricultural operations
An earthmoving skid steer used primarily for earth moving

explanations.a: A powered forklift used for material handling is a powered industrial truck. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: The workbook lists compressed air or nonflammable compressed gas-operated industrial trucks as not covered.
explanations.c: Farm vehicles are identified as not covered by 29 CFR 1910.178 in the workbook context.
explanations.d: Vehicles intended primarily for earth moving are not the same covered forklift category.

questions.name: Forklift Fundamentals and Markings
questions.objective: 1.2 Identify equipment covered and not covered by OSHA 1910.178
questions.text: Which item is identified as not covered by 29 CFR 1910.178 in the workbook?

answers.text: A counterbalanced forklift used for material handling
Vehicles intended primarily for earth moving, such as skid steers
A forklift equipped with forks for tiering pallets
A lift truck used to unload trailers

explanations.a: A material-handling forklift is within the powered industrial truck topic.
explanations.b: The workbook identifies earthmoving vehicles such as skid steers as outside 29 CFR 1910.178 coverage. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: A forklift used for tiering pallets is covered as powered industrial truck equipment.
explanations.d: A lift truck used for trailer unloading is a typical covered forklift use.

questions.name: Forklift Fundamentals and Markings
questions.objective: 1.2 Identify equipment covered and not covered by OSHA 1910.178
questions.text: Why can using earthmoving equipment for lifting be dangerous?

answers.text: It removes the need for stability evaluation
It makes load center irrelevant
It can become top-heavy and tip over when used for lifting outside its intended purpose
It always has a higher rated lifting capacity than a forklift

explanations.a: Stability concerns increase when equipment is used outside its intended purpose.
explanations.b: Answer boundary: load position and center of gravity remain important in lifting operations.
explanations.c: The workbook notes that vehicles primarily intended for earth moving can be dangerous for lifting because they can get top-heavy and tip over. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Higher capacity is not guaranteed, and the equipment may not be designed for that lift.

questions.name: Forklift Fundamentals and Markings
questions.objective: 1.3 Recognize design, construction, approval, and readable marking requirements
questions.text: What should be true about forklift nameplates and markings?

answers.text: They should be removed after attachments are installed
They may be painted over if the forklift is old
They must be present and readable
They are optional if the operator is experienced

explanations.a: Attachments may require updated markings, not removal of information.
explanations.b: Painting over markings can remove needed capacity and safety information.
explanations.c: Nameplates and markings provide critical information and must remain readable. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Experience does not replace readable markings.

questions.name: Forklift Fundamentals and Markings
questions.objective: 1.3 Recognize design, construction, approval, and readable marking requirements
questions.text: Which statement best addresses design approval and markings? Why are readable markings important to forklift operation?

answers.text: They make the forklift faster in narrow aisles
They replace the operator’s need to understand the load
They allow modifications without approval
They help operators verify capacity, approval information, and safe-use limits

explanations.a: Markings do not improve speed or maneuverability.
explanations.b: Operators still need to understand load weight, stability, and conditions.
explanations.c: Markings do not authorize unapproved modifications.
explanations.d: Readable plates and markings provide information operators need before safe operation. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Forklift Fundamentals and Markings
questions.objective: 1.3 Recognize design, construction, approval, and readable marking requirements
questions.text: What design and construction standard is referenced for forklifts in the workbook?

answers.text: ANSI/ITSDF B56.1 safety standard for low and high lift trucks
A traffic manual written for passenger cars
A warehouse inventory guide
A company-created checklist with no recognized standard

explanations.a: The workbook states forklift design and construction must comply with ANSI/ITSDF B56.1. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Forklift design and construction are not governed by passenger car traffic manuals.
explanations.c: Inventory guides do not establish forklift design requirements.
explanations.d: A checklist may help operations, but it is not the referenced design and construction standard.

questions.name: Forklift Fundamentals and Markings
questions.objective: 1.3 Recognize design, construction, approval, and readable marking requirements
questions.text: What does an approval label or identifying mark indicate?

answers.text: The operator is automatically certified to drive it
The forklift was approved for fire safety purposes by a nationally recognized testing laboratory
The forklift can safely lift any load in the workplace
The forklift no longer needs inspection

explanations.a: Truck approval is separate from operator training and evaluation.
explanations.b: The workbook explains that an approved forklift is listed or approved for fire safety purposes by a nationally recognized testing laboratory. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Approval markings do not override rated capacity or load limits.
explanations.d: Approval does not remove the need for inspection and maintenance.

questions.name: Forklift Fundamentals and Markings
questions.objective: 1.4 Identify safe practices for modifications, additions, data plates, and decals
questions.text: After an approved modification affects capacity or operation, what must be updated?

answers.text: Solely the paint color of the forklift
Capacity, operation, and maintenance instruction plates, tags, or decals
Solely the operator’s timecard
Solely the warehouse map

explanations.a: Paint color does not communicate revised capacity or operating limits.
explanations.b: When approved changes affect capacity or operation, plates, tags, and decals must be changed accordingly. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Timekeeping records do not update forklift safety information.
explanations.d: A map does not replace updated forklift plates, tags, or decals.

questions.name: Forklift Fundamentals and Markings
questions.objective: 1.4 Identify safe practices for modifications, additions, data plates, and decals
questions.text: During forklift operator certification training, which situation is unsafe?

answers.text: Updating the data plate after an approved capacity change
Reviewing operating instructions after a change
Using a forklift after an unapproved modification that changes safe operation
Following the manufacturer’s written approval process

explanations.a: Updated information helps operators use the forklift safely.
explanations.b: Reviewing instructions supports safe operation.
explanations.c: Unapproved changes can alter capacity, stability, controls, or safe-use limits. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Manufacturer approval is the required path for changes affecting safe operation.

questions.name: Forklift Fundamentals and Markings
questions.objective: 1.4 Identify safe practices for modifications, additions, data plates, and decals
questions.text: Why should data plates and decals match the forklift’s current configuration?

answers.text: They make manufacturer approval unnecessary
They are needed only for office recordkeeping
They are useful only when the forklift is parked
Operators rely on them for capacity, operating limits, and safety information

explanations.a: Current labels do not replace the approval requirement for modifications.
explanations.b: Data plates and decals support daily operation, not just records.
explanations.c: Operators use the information to make safe load and operation decisions.
explanations.d: Mismatch between equipment configuration and plates can lead to overload, instability, or improper use. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Forklift Fundamentals and Markings
questions.objective: 1.4 Identify safe practices for modifications, additions, data plates, and decals
questions.text: What must happen before a customer or user makes a modification that affects forklift capacity or safe operation?

The modification may be made first and documented later
The data plate may be ignored if the forklift still runs

questions.name: Forklift Fundamentals and Markings
questions.objective: 1.5 Recognize attachment marking and capacity effects
questions.text: During training, a supervisor is reviewing powered industrial truck safety. What must a nonmanufacturer front-end attachment be marked with?

answers.text: Identification of the attachment and the approximate combined weight of the forklift and attachment at maximum elevation with a centered load
A statement that the forklift capacity always increases
The date of the last lunch break
The operator’s preferred travel speed

explanations.a: The workbook states front-end attachments from sources other than the manufacturer must identify the attachment and list the approximate combined weight of the forklift and attachment at maximum elevation with a centered load. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Attachments can reduce capacity and must not be assumed to increase it.
explanations.c: Break timing is unrelated to attachment capacity marking.
explanations.d: Attachment markings focus on identification and weight/capacity information, not preferred speed.

questions.name: Forklift Fundamentals and Markings
questions.objective: 1.5 Recognize attachment marking and capacity effects
questions.text: How can special attachments affect forklift capacity?

answers.text: They remove the need to consider load center
They can reduce the maximum capacity of the forklift
They always make the forklift more stable
They make the data plate unnecessary

explanations.a: Load center remains important and may be affected by the attachment.
explanations.b: The workbook explains that special attachments instead of standard forks affect maximum capacity, often reducing it. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Attachments can move the load center and reduce stability.
explanations.d: Attachments increase the need to check capacity information.

questions.name: Forklift Fundamentals and Markings
questions.objective: 1.5 Recognize attachment marking and capacity effects
questions.text: A forklift is fitted with a clamp attachment. What should the operator verify before use?

answers.text: The forklift can lift the same maximum load as with standard forks
The attachment allows travel with loads raised high
The attachment is identified and the forklift’s current capacity information reflects the attachment
The attachment makes load weight irrelevant

explanations.a: Attachment use can reduce capacity and change stability.
explanations.b: Answer boundary: high travel with loads can increase tip-over risk.
explanations.c: Operators must understand how attachments affect capacity and safe operation before handling loads. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Load weight is still critical for capacity and stability.
